skeleton:
Butter-Basted Fried Eggs

British · Easy · Serves 2 (4 eggs)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The café's fried egg at its most controlled: eggs cracked into foaming butter and basted with the hot butter's spoonfuls — the whites setting evenly and the edges crisping gently rather than aggressively. Where the full English master's eggs fry in bacon fat (the fat economy's dividend), this master writes the butter-based version: the standalone breakfast egg, the component for the plate without the full English's meat, and the technique that gives the cook the most control over the white's set and the yolk's run.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The eggs

- The pan at medium heat before the butter goes in — the butter should foam on contact, not slowly melt (the foam is the temperature's confirmation). - The eggs cracked into individual cups or a bowl first — cracked directly into the pan, a broken yolk is unrecoverable.

Butter-Basted Fried Eggs

Prep: 1 minute · Cook: 3 minutes · Total: 4 minutes · Serves 2 (4 eggs)

Ingredients

The eggs

  • 4 large eggs (200 g), at room temperature
  • 30 g butter
  • 1 g fine sea salt
  • 5 g fresh chives, chopped (optional garnish)

Instructions

  1. The butter's foam. The butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat until it foams and the foam begins to subside — around 30 seconds. bubbles have begun to shrink — the pan is at the butter's ideal egg temperature (not the smoke point, which burns the butter's solids). Checkpoint — the butter has foamed and the foam's
  2. The eggs and the baste. The eggs gently tipped into the foaming butter, the heat dropped to medium-low, and the basting beginning: a spoon used to scoop the hot butter from the pan's edges and pour it over the egg whites' surfaces — repeatedly, for 2–3 minutes, until the whites are fully set and the edges have crisped in the butter's pool. (the basting cooks their tops without flipping), the edges are golden-crisp where they met the pan, and the yolks remain liquid under their barely-filmed surfaces — the basted egg's signature is the white's even set without the flip's risk. Checkpoint — the whites are opaque and just-set
  3. Serve immediately, salted, on buttered toast or beside the full English's other components. butter-crisp edge, then the yolk's run — the café's egg, complete in three minutes. Checkpoint — the first forkful runs the white's

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- Fried eggs wait for no one — 4 minutes from pan to plate. - The full English master's version replaces the butter with the accumulated bacon fat — the fat economy's richer route.

methodSteps.chefsNote: the basting method's advantage over the flip: the yolk never meets the pan, which means it stays liquid and pristine (the flip risks a broken yolk or an over-set bottom). The spoon's repeated pour over the whites does the flip's work from above — the hot butter cooking the white's surface as the pan cooks its bottom — and the egg arrives at the plate with both sides perfectly set and the yolk's dome intact.
